newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money ends little changed, gilts mixed.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money ends little changed, gilts mixed.

text.p: Indian call money ended Tuesday at 7.50-8.0 percent, slightly down from opening quotes of 7.75-8.25 percent, dealers said.
They said call money rates were firm throughout Tuesday with most of the day's trades at 8.0-8.25 percent.
Call money ended Monday at 3.25-3.5 percent but firmed up today on funds outflows.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) raised 50 billion rupees through an auction of four-year bonds on July 28 and successful bidders made payment today.
Dealers said they expect call money to remain firm at current levels through the week.

"The next repo auction on July 31 will determine whether call money rates come down," said a dealer at a private bank. "If the big lenders choose to roll over their repo, then it is unlikely call money will drop below 7.0 percent."
But some dealers said they expect call to ease on Wednesday as funds supply remains good.
"Rates are driven by sentiment and today lenders were able to keep rates high on the bond outflows," said a dealer.
"If one considers that the RBI received bids for 113 billion rupees (against a target of 50 billion) then it is clear that funds are still available in plenty."
Dealers said prices of government securities were mixed in active trade.

"Prices were up in the morning, then they came down when a primary dealer began selling stock in a big way," said a dealer. "But once he (the primary dealer) went off the market in the afternoon, prices recovered."
The 12.14 percent 2000 ended at 104.30, off the day's high of 104.45, but down from Monday's close of 104.32.
The 12.59 percent 2004 closed at 105.38, off the day's high of 105.50 compared to Monday's close of 105.08.
The 10.85 percent 2001 auctioned on Monday ended at 100.55, off an intraday high of 100.70.
